Zena Creek Steelhead Habitat Potential

Mike Ackerman

September 18, 2025

Currently, available spawning habitat for steelhead appears to be a limiting factor for production in Zena Creek. Adults are limited to spawning within the lower approximately 800 meters below the impoundment which is estimated to support only 3 steelhead redds (Table 1). Removing the current barrier would provide an additional 7002 meters of accessible spawning habitat supporting a potential of 23 additional redds (Table 1). Further, we estimate that the additional accessible habitat would provide a greater than 6-fold increase in available rearing habitat for steelhead fry and parr. Our evaluation of habitat capacity in Zena Creek uses results from the quantile random forest models described by See et al. (2021).

Table 1: Estimated habitat capacity for the current extent of available habitat to steelhead and potential accessible and suitable habitat if the impoundment were to be removed.
Status Model Stream Length (m) Capacity
current juv_sum 800 2,428
potential juv_sum 7,002 13,561
current redd 800 3
potential redd 7,002 23
